translations.idiomatic: Asked on his return how Shu fared, Xue Xu replied that the sovereign was blind to his faults, officials clung to silence, the court never heard honest speech, and the countryside showed famine in every face.

sentences.zh: 臣聞燕雀處堂，子母相樂，自以為安也，突決棟焚，而燕雀怡然不知禍之將及，其是之謂乎！」〉

translations.literal: “I have heard that swallows and sparrows in the hall, mother and young at play, think themselves secure; when the flue bursts and the rafters burn, the sparrows stay merry unaware that calamity draws near—is it not what we speak of!”〉
translations.idiomatic: “Swallows in the rafters,” he added, “nest and chirp while the chimney smolders—surely Shu is that heedless brood!”〉

sentences.zh: 子 瑩

translations.literal: Son Ying
translations.idiomatic: His younger son was Xue Ying.

sentences.zh: 惟臣之先，昔仕於漢，奕世綿綿，頗涉臺觀。

translations.literal: Only as for my ancestors, in former times they served Han; generation on generation endlessly, they quite trod the terraces and galleries.
translations.idiomatic: My forebears served the Han for generations and rose into the palace bureaucracy.

sentences.zh: 暨臣父綜，遭時之難，卯金失禦，邦家毀亂。

translations.literal: As for my father Zong, he encountered the hardship of the times: the Mao-Jin house lost the reins, state and family were ruined in chaos.
translations.idiomatic: My father Xue Zong lived when the Liu house lost the mandate and the empire shattered.

sentences.zh: 適茲樂土，庶存孑遺，天啟其心，東南是歸。

translations.literal: He reached this happy land, hoping barely to preserve what survived; Heaven opened his heart, and the southeast was his return.
translations.idiomatic: He found refuge in this happier south, clinging to life until Heaven turned his face toward the Wu court.

sentences.zh: 厥初流隸，困於蠻垂，大皇開基，恩德遠施。

translations.literal: At first cast as a wandering bondsman, trapped on the barbarian margin; the Grand Emperor opened the foundation, his kindness and favor reaching far.
translations.idiomatic: First he was a landless client on the barbarian frontier; then the Grand Emperor of Wu raised him from the mire and showered favor.

sentences.zh: 特蒙招命，拯擢泥污，釋放巾褐，受職剖符。

translations.literal: He alone received summons and mandate, was pulled from the mud and mire, released from cloth cap and coarse cloak, and received office with split tally.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned from obscurity, he shed commoner dress for silks, tally, and seal.

sentences.zh: 作守合浦，在海之隅，遷入京輦，遂升機樞。

translations.literal: He governed Hepu at the sea’s corner, moved into the capital region, then ascended the pivot’s hub.
translations.idiomatic: From governor of Hepu at the ocean’s edge he entered the capital and climbed to the inner councils.

sentences.zh: 枯瘁更榮，絕統復紀，自微而顯，非願之始。

translations.literal: Withered trunk flowered again, broken thread took up its weave—from slight to manifest, not what humble wishes at first intended.
translations.idiomatic: A dead branch bloomed anew, a snapped thread respooled—riches he had never dared dream.

sentences.zh: 亦惟寵遇，心存足止，重值文皇，建號東宮，乃作少傅，光華益隆。

translations.literal: Again he met favor, his heart knowing enough to stop; again he met the cultured emperor, who set up the Eastern Palace title, and made him Junior Tutor—splendor grew still greater.
translations.idiomatic: Twice favored, he knew when to be content; twice crowned with office—junior tutor when the Eastern Palace was founded—his glory redoubled.

sentences.zh: 明明聖嗣，至德謙祟，禮遇兼加，惟渥惟豐。

translations.literal: The brilliant holy heir, supreme virtue humble and lofty, doubled rites and courtesy, only rich, only abundant.
translations.idiomatic: The luminous heir-apparent, humble in supreme virtue, heaped rites and gifts upon him.

sentences.zh: 哀哀先臣，念竭其忠，洪恩未報，委世以終。

translations.literal: Alas for my late father, who thought to exhaust loyalty—the vast favor unrepaid, he yielded his generation and ended.
translations.idiomatic: Yet my father died with the dynasty’s debt to him still unpaid.

sentences.zh: 嗟臣蔑賤，惟昆及弟，幸生幸育，托綜遺體。

translations.literal: Woe is me, mean and low, only elder brother and younger brother—fortunate to be born and reared, relying on Zong’s surviving form.
translations.idiomatic: I, meanest of men, and my brothers owe our very bodies to Xue Zong’s line.

sentences.zh: 過庭既訓，頑蔽難啟。

translations.literal: Though he taught me in the courtyard, my dull obtuseness was hard to open.
translations.idiomatic: His courtyard lessons could not pierce my stubborn dullness.

sentences.zh: 堂構弗克，志存耦耕。

translations.literal: To shoulder the hall’s frame I could not; my aim was to plow side by side.
translations.idiomatic: I could not inherit his statesmanship; I only wished to farm in peace.

sentences.zh: 豈悟聖朝，仁澤流盈。

translations.literal: Who would have thought the holy court’s benevolent flood would overflow?
translations.idiomatic: I never dreamed the sacred court would flood us again with grace.

sentences.zh: 追錄先臣，愍其無成，是濟是拔，被以殊榮。

translations.literal: It traced my late father’s deeds, pitied his unfinished work, raised and pulled us up, draped us in singular glory.
translations.idiomatic: It remembered my father’s service, pitied his broken work, and lifted his sons with singular honors.

sentences.zh: 珝忝千里，受命南征，旌旗備物，金革揚聲。

translations.literal: Xu disgraced a command of a thousand li, received mandate to march south—banners and pennants complete, bronze and hide clanging.
translations.idiomatic: My brother Xue Xu bore a general’s baton a thousand li from home—full panoply, drums and mail ringing.

sentences.zh: 及臣斯陋，實暗實微，既顯前軌，人物之機。

translations.literal: As for me, mean and dim, truly dull and slight, yet shown the former track, the pivot of men and affairs.
translations.idiomatic: I, coarse and dim, was still shown the path my father walked—the hinge of men and policy.

sentences.zh: 復傅東宮，繼世荷輝，才不逮先，是忝是違。

translations.literal: Again tutor to the Eastern Palace, inheriting favor generation on generation—talent not matching the ancestor, thus shamed, thus failing.
translations.idiomatic: Again named tutor to the heir, I inherit favor I cannot repay—talent far short of my father’s, I stand ashamed.

sentences.zh: 乾德博好，文雅是貴，追悼亡臣，冀存遺類。

translations.literal: The Qian virtue broadly loves, taking letters and refinement as precious, mourning the dead minister, hoping to preserve what he left behind.
translations.idiomatic: Your Qian virtue cherishes letters and mourns the dead minister, hoping to keep his seed alive.

sentences.zh: 如何愚胤，曾無彷彿！

translations.literal: How could my foolish descendant be so unlike him!
translations.idiomatic: Yet how unlike him is this foolish son!

sentences.zh: 瞻彼舊寵，顧此頑虛，孰能忍愧，臣實與居。

translations.literal: Gazing on that old favor, turning to this stubborn void—who can bear the shame? Your servant shares it.
translations.idiomatic: I look from his old honors to my hollow self—who could bear the shame? I cannot.

sentences.zh: 夙夜反側，克心自論，父子兄弟，累世蒙恩，死惟結草，生誓殺身，雖則灰隕，無報萬分。

translations.literal: Day and night I toss, examining my heart: father and son, elder and younger brother, piled blessings through generations—dead I would tie grass, living I swear to give my life; though I crumble to ash, I cannot repay the myriad part.
translations.idiomatic: Night and day I turn on my mat: our house has piled up grace life after life—dead, I would tie the knot of gratitude; living, I would give my marrow—yet ash could not repay the debt.

sentences.zh: 是歲，何定建議鑿聖谿以通江淮，皓令瑩督萬人往，遂以多盤石難施功，罷還，出為武昌左部督，後定被誅，皓追聖谿事，下瑩獄，徙廣州。

translations.literal: That year He Ding proposed digging the Sheng Creek to link the Yangzi and Huai; Hao ordered Ying to supervise ten thousand men to go; because there were many boulders progress was hard, they stopped and returned; he went out as Colonel of the Left in Wuchang; later when Ding was executed Hao traced the Sheng Creek affair, cast Ying into prison, and banished him to Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: That year He Ding urged cutting the Sheng Creek channel between the Yangzi and Huai; Sun Hao put Xue Ying in charge of ten thousand laborers until boulders stalled the work. After Ying was demoted to colonel of the left at Wuchang, He Ding’s execution brought the canal scandal back to light—Hao jailed Ying and shipped him to Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 右國史華核上疏曰：

translations.literal: Right National Historian Hua He submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Right national historian Hua He answered with a memorial:

sentences.zh: 臣聞五帝三王皆立史官，敘錄功美，垂之無窮。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that the Five Emperors and Three Kings all established historiographers, recording merit and beauty to hang endless.
translations.idiomatic: I have read that every sage-king kept scribes to set down deeds for posterity.

sentences.zh: 漢時司馬遷、班固，咸命世大才，所撰精妙，與六經俱傳。

translations.literal: In Han, Sima Qian and Ban Gu were both world-ordering great talents; what they compiled was subtle and passed down with the Six Classics.
translations.idiomatic: Han’s Sima Qian and Ban Gu were geniuses of their age; their histories rank beside the classics.

sentences.zh: 大吳受命，建國南土。

translations.literal: Great Wu received the Mandate and built the state in the southern soil.
translations.idiomatic: Great Wu took the mandate and planted its capital in the southern soil.

sentences.zh: 大皇帝末年，命太史令丁孚、郎中項峻始撰《吳書》。

translations.literal: In the Grand Emperor’s late years he ordered Astrologer-royal Ding Fu and Gentleman of the Household Xiang Jun to begin compiling the Book of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Grand Emperor’s reign he set Ding Fu and Xiang Jun to drafting the *Book of Wu*.

sentences.zh: 孚、峻俱非史才，其所撰作，不足紀錄。

translations.literal: Fu and Jun both lacked historian talent; what they wrote was not worth recording.
translations.idiomatic: Neither man had a historian’s gift; their draft was not worth preserving.

sentences.zh: 至少帝時，更差韋曜、周昭、薛瑩、梁廣及臣五人，訪求往事，所共撰立，備有本末。

translations.literal: By at least the Lesser Emperor’s time he reassigned Wei Yao, Zhou Zhao, Xue Ying, Liang Guang, and your servant—five men—to inquire into past events and jointly establish a draft, complete from beginning to end.
translations.idiomatic: The Lesser Emperor later added Wei Yao, Zhou Zhao, Xue Ying, Liang Guang, and myself—five scholars—to comb the archives and assemble a full chronicle.

sentences.zh: 昭、廣先亡，曜負恩蹈罪，瑩出為將，復以過徙，其書遂委滯，迄今末撰奏。

translations.literal: Zhou and Guang died first; Yao requited favor with crime; Ying went out as a general, then was banished again for fault—the book therefore stalled and to this day has not been finished and presented.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Zhao and Liang Guang died early; Wei Yao fell to treason; Xue Ying was sent out as a general and then exiled for fault—the manuscript stalled and has still not been completed and memorialized.

sentences.zh: 臣愚淺才劣，適可為瑩等記注而已，若使撰合，必襲孚、峻之跡，懼墜大皇帝之元功，損當世之盛美。

translations.literal: Your servant is foolish and shallow, talent poor—fit only to assist Ying and others with notes; if charged to compile jointly, he would surely follow Fu and Jun’s tracks, fearing to drop the Grand Emperor’s primal deeds and diminish the age’s splendor.
translations.idiomatic: I am too shallow to do more than annotate for Xue Ying; if forced to compile, I would repeat Ding Fu’s failure and blot the Grand Emperor’s glory.

sentences.zh: 瑩涉學既博，文章尤妙，同寮之中，瑩為冠首。

translations.literal: Ying’s learning ranges wide and his writing especially fine—among peers he is chief.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Ying’s erudition is vast and his prose the finest of our circle.

sentences.zh: 今者見吏，雖多經學，記述之才，如瑩者少，是以慺慺為國惜之。

translations.literal: Among present clerks many have classical learning, but few have narrative talent like Ying; therefore I earnestly grieve for the state over losing him.
translations.idiomatic: Plenty of officials know the classics; almost none can narrate like he—hence my fear for the history itself.

sentences.zh: 實欲使卒垂成之功，編於前史之末。

translations.literal: I truly wish to see the nearly finished work appended to the end of prior histories.
translations.idiomatic: Let him finish the book and append it to the dynastic record—that is my plea.

sentences.zh: 奏上之後，退填溝壑，無所復恨。

translations.literal: After the memorial is submitted I may retreat to fill ditches and gullies with no further regret.
translations.idiomatic: Once it is done I may die in a ditch without regret.

sentences.zh: 皓遂召瑩還，為左國史。

translations.literal: Hao thereupon summoned Ying back as Left National Historian.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hao recalled Xue Ying as left national historian.

sentences.zh: 頃之，選曹尚書同郡繆禕以執意不移，為群小所疾，左遷衡陽太守。

translations.literal: Before long Director of Personnel Miao Yi of the same commandery, because he would not shift his resolve, was envied by petty men and demoted Administrator of Hengyang.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, Miao Yi of the same bureau—stubborn in principle—was slandered into the governorship of Hengyang.

sentences.zh: 既拜，又追以職事見詰責，拜表陳謝。

translations.literal: After his appointment he was further pressed with duties in interrogation; he submitted a memorial of apology.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned to account for his conduct, he filed a humble apology.

sentences.zh: 因過詣瑩，復為人所白，雲禕不懼罪，多將賓客會聚瑩許，乃收禕下獄，徙桂陽，瑩還廣州。

translations.literal: On his way he called on Ying and was again denounced—that Yi did not fear guilt but gathered many guests at Ying’s place—whereupon Yi was seized and imprisoned, banished to Guiyang, Ying returned to Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Stopping to visit Xue Ying, he was accused of plotting; Yi went to jail in Guiyang while Ying was sent back to Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 未至，召瑩還，復職。

translations.literal: Before he reached his post, [Hao] summoned Ying back and restored his office.
translations.idiomatic: Ying had not reached exile when the emperor recalled him to office.

sentences.zh: 是時法政多謬，舉措煩苛，瑩每上便宜，陳緩刑簡役，以濟育百姓，事或施行。

translations.literal: At that time laws and government had many errors and acts were vexingly harsh; Ying often submitted what was fitting, urging lighter punishments and simpler corvée to nourish the hundred surnames—sometimes adopted.
translations.idiomatic: As Wu’s laws grew cruel and petty, Ying repeatedly urged lighter penalties and shorter labor levies to spare the people—some of it heeded.

sentences.zh: 遷光祿勳。

translations.literal: He was promoted Supernumerary Household Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to supernumerary household grandee.

sentences.zh: 天紀四年，督軍征皓，皓奉書司馬由、王渾、王濬請降，其文，瑩所造也。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianji the army supervising the expedition against Hao—Hao submitted letters to Sima You, Wang Hun, and Wang Jun seeking surrender; the text was composed by Ying.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianji 4, when the Jin commanders marched against Sun Hao, Hao sent surrender letters to Sima You, Wang Hun, and Wang Jun—Xue Ying drafted every line.

sentences.zh: 瑩既至洛陽，特先見敘，為散騎常侍，答問處當，皆有條理。

translations.literal: When Ying reached Luoyang he was granted audience first and made Supernumerary Gentleman Cavalryman-at-attendance, answering questions with orderly structure.
translations.idiomatic: At Luoyang he was received before other captives, named supernumerary gentleman cavalry attendant, and answered the Jin court’s questions with crisp logic.

sentences.zh: 〈干寶《晉紀》曰：武帝從容問瑩曰：「孫皓之所以亡者何也？

translations.literal: Gan Bao’s Jin ji states: The Martial Emperor casually asked Ying, “What was the reason Sun Hao perished?”
translations.idiomatic: Gan Bao’s *Jin ji* records Emperor Wu asking Xue Ying what brought Sun Hao down.

sentences.zh: 」瑩對曰：「歸命侯臣皓之君吳也，暱近小人，刑罰妄加，大臣大將，無所親信，人人憂恐，各不自保，危亡之釁，實由於此。

translations.literal: Ying answered, saying: “When the Marquis Who Surrendered His Mandate, Sun Hao, ruled Wu, he favored petty men, punishments were applied at random, great ministers and great generals had none in whom he placed trust; every man lived in worry and terror, each unable to keep himself secure—the flaw of peril and ruin truly arose from this.”
translations.idiomatic: Xue Ying answered that when Sun Hao—already reduced to the surrendered “marquis who handed over his fate”—still ruled Wu, he surrounded himself with small men, lashed out with arbitrary penalties, and trusted neither his chief ministers nor his field commanders, so that everyone lived in dread and no one felt safe; the seeds of Wu’s fall lay there.

sentences.zh: 」帝遂問吳士存亡者之賢愚，瑩各以狀對。〉

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon asked about worthy and foolish among Wu scholars who survived or had died; Ying answered each according to circumstance.〉
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu went on to ask which Wu scholars still living or dead had been worthy or wanting, and Ying gave him a candid report on each.〉

sentences.zh: 太康三年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the third year of Taikang.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Taikang 3 (282 CE).

sentences.zh: 著書八篇，名曰《新議》。

translations.literal: He composed eight treatises, entitled New Discussions.
translations.idiomatic: He left eight essays collected under the title *New Discussions*.

sentences.zh: 〈王隱《晉書》曰：瑩子兼，字令長，清素有器宇，資望故如上國，不似吳人。

translations.literal: Wang Yin’s Jin shu states: Ying’s son Jian, courtesy Lingzhang, was pure and plain, with bearing and capacity; his talent and reputation were like those of the central states—not like a man of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yin’s *Jin shu* adds that Xue Jian, courtesy Lingzhang, was austere and dignified, with the polish of a capital scholar rather than a southerner.

sentences.zh: 歷位二宮丞相長史。

translations.literal: He successively held office as chief clerk to the chancellor in the Two Palaces.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the chief clerkships under the Jin chancellors of the Two Palaces.

sentences.zh: 元帝踐阼，累遷丹楊尹、尚書，又為太子少傅。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yuan ascended the throne, he was promoted in stages to Governor of Danyang and Palace Attendant, and again became Junior Tutor to the Heir.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Yuan took the throne, Xue Jian climbed step by step to governor of Danyang, palace attendant, and once more junior tutor to the heir.

sentences.zh: 自綜至兼，三世傅東宮。〉

translations.literal: From Zong to Jian, three generations tutored the Eastern Palace.〉
translations.idiomatic: From Xue Zong to Xue Jian, three generations of the family tutored the crown prince.〉

sentences.zh: 作者評論

translations.literal: Author’s commentary
translations.idiomatic: Author’s appraisal

sentences.zh: 評曰：張紘文理意正，為世令器，孫策待之亞於張昭，誠有以也，嚴、程、闞生，一時儒林也。

translations.literal: The appraisal states: Zhang Hong’s literary pattern and meaning were correct; he was a fine vessel for the age; Sun Ce treated him next after Zhang Zhao—there was real reason for it. Yan, Cheng, and Kan in their day stood among the grove of scholars.
translations.idiomatic: The historian’s verdict: Zhang Hong combined sound doctrine with principled judgment—a statesman the age could use; that Sun Ce ranked him just below Zhang Zhao was no accident. Yan Jun, Cheng Bing, and Kan Ze belonged to the best scholarly cohort of their time.

sentences.zh: 至畯辭榮濟舊，不亦長者乎！

translations.literal: As for Jun declining honor to rescue an old friend—is he not an elder worthy!
translations.idiomatic: Yan Jun’s refusal of high office to save an old friend marks him as a true elder in the best sense.

sentences.zh: 薛綜學識規納，為吳良臣。

translations.literal: Xue Zong’s learning, knowledge, standards, and acceptance made him a good minister of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Zong’s erudition, judgment, and openness to counsel made him one of Wu’s ablest ministers.

sentences.zh: 及瑩纂蹈，允有先風，然於暴酷之朝，屢登顯列，君子殆諸。

translations.literal: When it came to Ying’s editorial work and following in his father’s path, he fully bore his ancestor’s manner; yet in a cruel and violent court he repeatedly ascended to eminent ranks—a gentleman may well feel uneasy about that.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Ying, carrying on his father’s historical work and example, lived up to the family tradition, yet he rose again and again under a brutal tyrant—something that would give any scrupulous observer pause.
